title: Add introspection record, class registry, and status review (step 1)
summary: Implements build-order step 1 of defaults-loop.md §12: an event-triggered athena.introspection/1 record (rejected or failed job, correction, intervention), a class registry record store, and code that reads records/ per §3.3 and passes a filtered summary to a language model for the prose. The record shows in `athena status <job>`. It reuses backtest's schema, records reader, citation validation and evidence-after-decision rule by moving them to shared code, with no Jev. Tests use fixture records in a temp directory.

defaults_applied.how: Reuse backtest's reader, schema and validation, and existing crates (serde, jiff); build nothing a crate already covers.
Fixture tests in a temp directory; cargo test passes and clippy is clean.
Status output is exercised by a test running the CLI path.
Doc comments and the CHANGELOG are written for an outside reader.
Fixtures use synthetic data, with no personal data.
Step 1 only; steps 2 to 6 are excluded.
The shared code is extracted rather than copied, so there is one reader and one schema.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Without Jev, failure_class and prevention_kind are chosen by code or the language model from the registry, with `new` plus a proposed name when nothing fits; the choice is marked as not from Jev.
The language model call goes through the existing athena-agent abstraction, with a fake agent in tests.
A failed introspection is recorded as failed, never blocks the job, and is not itself introspected.
Host-error and landing triggers (§3.1 rows 5 and 6) and retry-from-record (§3.5) are step 2 or later and are left out.
Rejected proposals and plans have no record yet, so they are not triggers here.
The 'person-visible review' is the introspection block in `athena status <job>` plus its --json form; no separate review command.
Shared reader and introspection types move from athena-cli backtest.rs into a lower crate (athena-data or athena-core) that both backtest and the new code use; backtest output is unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.text: The athena.introspection/1 schema, the records reader and the citation validation exist once, in shared code used by both `athena backtest` and the new introspection path; backtest.rs keeps no duplicate definition.
A class registry record store exists. New classes are added as `proposed` with a code-assigned id, and the repository files are never edited.

The §3.3 reading code reads only the listed stored fields (never transcripts, diffs or other jobs' files). It narrows by class_of_work and category, caps earlier cases at 5, and passes only those fields to the model.
On return, any earlier_cases or decisions_matched id not on the list passed in is dropped and logged. A cause equal to what_happened after normalising is flagged and the record rated failed.
Introspection is triggered automatically for a rejected job, a failed job, a correction and any other intervention. It is not triggered for a failed introspection.
Evidence is checked to be after the decision it is cited against, using the existing backtest rule.
`athena status <job>` prints the introspection (what happened, class, earlier cases, cause, prevention, proposed request, status) and includes it in --json.

Run `cargo test`: fixture-record tests in a temp directory pass. They cover each trigger, class matching and new-class creation, id dropping, cause-restates-event flagging, the failed-introspection path, and the status output. The existing backtest tests still pass unchanged.
Run `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean.
A docs note, and a CHANGELOG entry, say that step 1 is built and that the run over real records follows landing.

out_of_scope: Jev client or any call to POST /v1/evaluate
Proposal records, `athena status` surfacing of proposals, apply-as-a-job (step 3)
Host-error and landing triggers, and a record for rejected proposals or plans
Running over the real records/ directory
Changes to defaults.toml, athena.toml, CI or lint configuration
departures: The reference is computed from smaller jobs. This one spans several crates, adds a refactor of backtest, a new record, a trigger in the job lifecycle, a model call and status output, so I expect higher cost, longer time and a lower pass rate.
